sentences.text: At the very outset Sri Romit Seth has stated that this is a peculiar case wherein the petitioner no. 1 is extending all financial and other possible help to his first wife namely, Ms. Tarannum Bano who is daughter of opposite party no. 4 and also despite the fact that after taking divorce from her he remarried and taking care of her properly but her father, opposite party no. 4, has lodged a false and misconceived F.I.R. against him indicating the date of incident on which he was away from India.
He has also stated that his second wife is now pregnant at this time and if the petitioner no. 1 is compelled to face the proceedings he may suffer irreparable loss.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has also informed that his first wife after taking divorce from him has herself remarried with someone else, from whom she has taken divorce and now has remarried with the present petitioner.

Therefore, the impugned proceedings are an outcome of matrimonial dispute and also having a peculiar nature, therefore, it appears that the aforesaid dispute may be settled by the parties amicably through Mediation and Conciliation Center of this Court.
7. Law is trite that before sending any matter to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre, consent of the parties would be required.

8. So as to show the bonafide, the petitioner no. 1 is ready to deposit a sum of Rs.
50,000/- within a period of one month before the Mediation and Conciliation Center of this Court.

If the daughter of opposite party no. 4 namely, Ms. Tarannum Bano,
who shall be appearing on the next date, agrees to settle the dispute amicably through Mediation and Conciliation Center, a sum of Rs. 45,000/- be given to her but if she does not agree to settle the dispute amicably, the amount in question may not be paid to her.
Therefore, the aforesaid aspect may be considered on the next date when the parties would be appearing before this Court.
9. Therefore, list this case on 15.2.2024.

On that date the petitioner no. 1 and daughter of opposite party no. 4 along with opposite party no. 4 shall appear in person for the purposes of giving their consent as to whether the matter be sent to Mediation and Conciliation Center of this Court for settling the dispute amicably.

4. In compliance of the aforesaid order, Sri Ashfak Khan O.P. No.4 along with his daughter Ms.
Tarannum Bano, are present in person.
No one has appeared on behalf of the petitioners nor the petitioner No.1 is present.
No request for adjournment etc., has been made on behalf of the petitioner No.1.
5. Sri Satyendra Kumar Singh Sub-Inspector, PS Kotwali district Sultanpur has ensured the present of O.P. No.4 and his daughter.
6. The ordersheet reveals that despite the fact that the petitioner No.1 was ready to deposit a sum of Rs.50,000/- but he has not deposited the aforesaid amount of Rs.50,000/-.
Therefore, it appears that the petitioners are not interested to contest this case.
7. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
Interim order is vacated.
The learned Trial Court is directed to take appropriate coercive steps against the petitioners if they do not cooperate in the proceedings.
8. Learned counsel for the O.P. No.4 may intimate this order to the learned Trial Court.
